title: perf(canary): add automated latency/throughput regression detector + rollout guards
author: Jasper Lin
description:
Motivation: We observed occasional regressions slipping into canary rollouts when load characteristics shift. This PR introduces an automated detector that monitors latency and throughput time-series from the perf-canary harness and blocks rollouts when statistically significant regressions are detected.

What this change does: Adds a detector service (perf-canary/detector) that computes baseline distributions, runs continuous KS/Wilcoxon checks on p95/p99 latency and throughput, and exposes a verdict API consumed by the rollout guard controller. The rollout controller has conservative default thresholds and a hysteresis window to avoid flapping.

Checklist: 
- [x] Detector core algorithm and config
- [x] Canary harness integration (ingest + labeling)
- [x] Rollout guard controller integration in ops/rollout
- [x] CI e2e test that injects synthetic latency regressions
- [x] Docs describing tuning knobs and mitigation paths

Testing: Unit tests for statistical checks, integration tests in tests/perf_canary that simulate baseline vs regressed runs, and a CI workflow (ci/workflows/perf-canary.yml) that runs the e2e canary under short-lived infra. One flaky test (ingest backfill) was fixed by increasing the retry backoff.

Backward compatibility: The detector is opt-in via canary profile annotation; existing rollouts default to previous behavior. Operators can enable strict block or warn-only modes.

Notes: This PR focuses on latency/throughput regressions; quality regressions (model output drift) will be in a follow-up (ENG-4227).
commits: feat(perf-canary): add detector service and verdict API
feat(ops/rollout): integrate rollout guard to query perf verdicts
test(perf-canary): add e2e regression injection and harness scripts
ci: add perf-canary workflow and required secrets/config
docs: perf-canaries.md describing thresholds, hysteresis, and ops playbook
chore: lint and type fixes after reviewer feedback
review_comments: Monica Reyes (reviewer): Looks solid overall. Please add a short note about warmup bias in the detector; early tokens can inflate p95. Suggest adding a warmup exclusion window (e.g., first 5 minutes).
Jasper Lin (author): Added warmup exclusion in defaults.yaml and documented rationale in perf-canaries.md. Also added a flag to turn exclusion off for very short canaries.

Aisha Khan (reviewer): Can we make the default mode "warn-only" for the first 48 hours after enabling? Ops prefer conservative rollouts. Also request clearer logs when a check is skipped due to low sample size.
Jasper Lin (author): Implemented warn-only grace period and added explicit log lines. Updated tests to assert warn-only behavior.
Luca Moretti (reviewer): Minor: use context with timeout in guard_controller to avoid blocking goroutines if detector is slow. Also please squash the small lint commits.

Jasper Lin (author): Added context timeout and rebased/squashed history. CI rerun after fix passed.

Final approval given by Monica Reyes.
ci_summary: Main CI: pass (unit + linters), Perf-canary workflow: pass after one rerun (intermittent ingest backfill failure fixed). CodeQL: pass.
release_notes: Add automated perf-canary detector and rollout guards. Default is opt-in; operators can enable block or warn-only modes. Includes docs with tuning guidance and an e2e test harness.
notes_for_ops: Defaults live in perf-canary/config/defaults.yaml. Key knobs: p_value_threshold, min_sample_size, hyst_window_seconds, warmup_exclusion_seconds, post_enable_grace_seconds (warn-only). If a canary is blocked, operator can: 1) set mode=warn-only, 2) increase min_sample_size, 3) re-run canary with controlled load to confirm. See docs/perf-canaries.md for playbook.
risk_assessment: Medium: introduces automated blocking logic. Default is opt-in and warn-only grace period reduces blast radius. Added extensive tests and conservative defaults. Ops rollback path documented.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): automated detector for latency and throughput regressions + rollout guards (opt-in)
